objective: Provide a bounded, reproducible operating procedure for demonstrating raw ZTF DR24 light-curve acquisition, inspection, diagnostic QC, provenance, and export without claiming validated classifier behavior.

previous_knowledge_consumed.detail: The Park prototype requires a working scientist-facing workflow and dated evidence. The 30–50-object guided demonstration is a target, not a verified current capability.
The raw DR24 Explorer is distinct from the default ALeRCE observation and inference path. Source identity, filter grouping, normalization, and production QC remain separate acceptance requirements.
The Explorer supports bounded 1–10 OID raw inspection and JSON export. Its QC is diagnostic only; it does not run the frozen v0.2.0 model.
The PR failed because the documentation change had no cumulative cycle record. Test Suite, Runtime Smoke, Package Build, and Dependency Audit were skipped after the lifecycle gate failed.

baseline.description: The repository contains a raw DR24 Explorer and a bounded live API parity test. The two-OID live test and local Workbench run described by this runbook have not yet been verified for this Park handoff.

change.scope: Consolidate the Park runbook, full-cohort acceptance contract, parallel dataset plan, current handbook, master roadmap, defect register, think-tank review, Persian Park status addendum, installation/quick-start/user documentation, model card, scientific methodology, source adapters, architecture identity boundary, and production acceptance checklist. No model weights, baseline, feature schema, taxonomy, thresholds, or production data are changed.
change.rationale: A bounded, raw-preserving demonstration can show real-data retrieval and provenance while avoiding unsupported claims about physical identity, production QC, DR24 classifier inference, calibrated probabilities, or anomaly discovery.

reproducibility.before: Park operation depended on informal knowledge and did not have one versioned, bounded operator procedure.
reproducibility.after: The runbook records the checkout, Python 3.11 environment, pinned OIDs, live API parity test, Workbench steps, evidence retention, and claim boundaries.

scientific_validity.before: A presentation could conflate raw DR24 inspection with classifier inference and scientific validation.
scientific_validity.after: The runbook explicitly limits demonstrated claims to raw DR24 retrieval, inspection, diagnostic QC, provenance, and export.

reliability.before: The pinned two-OID live test and local Workbench path have no verified acceptance record for this handoff.
reliability.after: Both operations must pass and produce retained evidence before the demonstrator is accepted.

measurement.trade_off: The bounded raw-data demonstration is narrower than the complete classifier and discovery platform described in the long-term product vision. This limitation is explicit and intentional.

validation.blocker: Run the pinned live source-parity test and the local Workbench procedure on a clean isolated Python 3.11 checkout; retain commit SHA, full output, screenshot, exported JSON, and SHA-256. The full-cohort Park acceptance remains open.
blockers: Do not accept a failed or skipped live source-parity test.
Verify that both OIDs are returned with 78 and 123 epochs and their pinned payload hashes.
Verify separate g- and r-band OID panels, raw table, diagnostic QC, provenance, and JSON export in the Workbench.
Do not claim classifier inference, calibrated probabilities, physical-source identity, production QC, or scientific anomaly discovery from this demonstration.

root_causes: The documentation-only PR added a meaningful file under docs/acceptance/ but did not include the required machine-readable cumulative cycle record.
The lifecycle gate therefore failed and downstream CI stages were skipped.
The local live-data and Workbench acceptance operations remain unverified for this handoff.

findings: A real-data raw Explorer is a valid laboratory demonstration only when its claim boundary is explicit.
A source-parity test and a visible Workbench screen are separate acceptance evidence.
A successful scientific-validation workflow that skips source-backed jobs does not establish source-backed scientific validation.
Raw survey OIDs must remain separate until a validated physical-source identity rule exists.

open_blockers: Run the complete current-head CI after adding this cycle record.
Execute the pinned DR24 live source-parity test.
Execute the Workbench workflow and verify the exported evidence package.
Review the Park presentation so current raw-Explorer capabilities are not described as validated classifier outputs.

knowledge_carried_forward: The v0.2.0 scientific baseline and baseline_v0.2 model identity remain unchanged.
The CPVS membership discrepancy remains a separate unresolved research issue and is not a blocker for this bounded raw-data demonstrator.
The DR24 Explorer remains experimental and diagnostic-only.
The Park demonstrator is not accepted until the live source-parity test and local Workbench run pass.
Do not publish a Park demo release or claim full classifier readiness before the acceptance evidence is complete.
The Park laboratory demonstrator and the full Park MVP are separate gates.
Current main CI success is engineering evidence only; 13 tests remain skipped and the original production model artifact is unavailable.
The 150-row DR24 Objects Table and 150-row ALeRCE reference snapshots are independent, unpaired evidence sets.
All current product and Park claims must follow the 2026-11-19 handbook and Persian technical addendum.
